title: Angle Properties of Circles
seo_title: Sec 3 Angle properties of circles Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: angle properties of circles: angle in a semicircle is a right angle; angle between tangent and radius is a right angle; angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference; angles in the same segment are equal; angles in opposite segments are supplementary
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on angle properties of circles: angle at the centre, angle in a semicircle, tangent and radius, angles in the same segment and cyclic quadrilaterals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
key_sub: Angle in a semicircle = 90°; same segment angles are equal; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

  • The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
  • The angle in a semicircle is 90°, and the angle between a tangent and a radius is 90°.
  • Angles in the same segment (standing on the same arc) are equal.
  • Angles in opposite segments add up to 180°: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
  • Look for radii: OA = OB makes an isosceles triangle.
Example

∠APB = 38° at the circumference. Find ∠AOB at the centre.

Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference

Answer: 76°

Example

ABCD is cyclic and ∠A = 104°. Find ∠C.

Opposite angles add to 180°

Answer: 76°

Common mistakes

  • Halving when you should double (and the other way round).
  • Using 180° instead of 90° for the angle in a semicircle.
  • Adding opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral to 360°.
  • Missing the isosceles triangle formed by two radii.

faq.q: What are the angle properties of circles?
faq.a: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, the angle in a semicircle is 90°, angles in the same segment are equal, opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°, and a tangent meets a radius at 90°.
A quadrilateral with all four vertices on a circle. Its opposite angles add up to 180°.

faq.q: What does 'angles in the same segment' mean?
faq.a: Angles at the circumference that stand on the same chord or arc, on the same side of it. They are always equal.

faq.q: How do I give reasons in a circle proof?

items.e: OB = OC (radii), so ∠OCB = ∠OBC. ∠ACB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠ABC = 90° − 48° = 42°. ∠OCB = 42°.
